source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Radico Khaitan is a domestic Indian spirits (IMFL) company. Small export business exists — premium brands Rampur Indian Single Malt Whisky and Jaisalmer Indian Craft Gin exported to 85+ countries (US, Europe, Middle East, Southeast Asia) — but estimated <10% of standalone revenue. FY25 standalone revenue ₹4,851 Cr (+19% YoY). No China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative found in FY25 IR communications.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~8% of standalone revenue (₹4,851 Cr FY25). Premium brands sold in US, Europe, Middle East and Southeast Asia. Exact USD-denominated share not separately disclosed; bulk of exports to multiple currency markets.

china_plus_one.evidence: Schaeffler India exports ~10% of revenue as intercompany supplies to Schaeffler Group globally. India serves primarily domestic Indian auto OEM market. EV segment grew to 25.2% of CY2025 revenue (from 8.05% in CY2023). CY2025 net revenue ₹9,395 Cr (+16.3% YoY). No explicit China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative identified in available communications. Calendar-year reporting company.

inr_exposure.evidence: Intercompany exports ~10% of revenue to Schaeffler Group globally. CY2025 total revenue ₹9,395 Cr. Domestic auto OEM business (bearings, precision components) ~90% of revenue. Schaeffler India is a calendar-year company; CY2025 annual report is most recent.

china_plus_one.evidence: BEL is a 100% government-owned Navratna defence PSU. Export turnover USD 106M in FY25 (~3.8% of ₹23,024 Cr total revenue). All revenue from GoI defence procurement. No China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative — defence equipment sold to Indian Armed Forces, DRDO, and allied friendly nations.

govt_capex.evidence: BEL is 100% government-owned Navratna defence PSU. All revenue from defence procurement by Indian Armed Forces, DRDO, and government agencies. FY25 revenue ₹23,024 Cr (+16% YoY); defence segment 89.75% of revenue; non-defence (civilian electronics, networking, homeland security) 10.25%. Order book ~₹74,000 Cr (from FY26 announcements). Key products: radar systems, electronic warfare, C4I systems, fire control, night vision devices, communication systems.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export turnover USD 106M in FY25 (~3.8% of total revenue), up 14% YoY from USD 92.98M. Exports grew further to USD 141.9M in FY26. Defence equipment exported to friendly nations; government-to-government agreements.

china_plus_one.evidence: Siemens India operates predominantly in domestic market across Smart Infrastructure, Mobility (Railways), Digital Industries, and Low Voltage Motors segments. Exports minimal (~3-4% intercompany). No China+1 narrative — primary demand driver is India's infrastructure-led domestic capex cycle. Note: Siemens India changed fiscal year from Sep-end to Apr-Mar; FY2023-24 refers to Oct 2023–Sep 2024 (last completed Sep-end annual report); 18-month transitional period Oct 2024–Mar 2026 may be published imminently.

govt_capex.evidence: Siemens India's Mobility segment (railway electrification, signalling, locomotives) and Smart Infrastructure (power distribution, building technology, smart cities) are heavily government capex-driven. Q4 FY2024 (Sep-qtr): Smart Infrastructure ₹2,725 Cr, Mobility ₹1,135 Cr. Government capex in railways, metro, power distribution, water, and urban infrastructure is primary demand driver. Siemens management cites continued government capex as key growth outlook driver. Exact government capex revenue % not separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Primarily domestic operations; FY2023-24 (Oct23–Sep24) consolidated revenue ~₹22,000 Cr. TTM revenue as of Apr 2026 ₹18,968 Cr. Siemens India transitioning to Apr-Mar fiscal year; 18-month transitional period Oct'24–Mar'26.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Nippon Life India AMC revenue is management fees linked to AUM (~₹4.5 lakh Cr in FY25 including alternates). Interest rate changes materially affect AUM composition (debt vs equity allocation) and net fund inflows. Falling rates typically boost debt fund AUM; rising rates may redirect savings to fixed deposits. Company itself has minimal debt (floating rate liabilities ~nil). FY25 revenue ₹2,709 Cr, PAT ₹1,529 Cr (+18.85% YoY), AUM grew 29% in FY25, investor folios 1.07 Cr as of Sep-25.

inr_exposure.evidence: 100% domestic Asset Management Company. All revenue INR-denominated mutual fund management fees. No USD or foreign currency exposure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield exports to 50+ countries with volumes growing ~30% YoY; export revenue reached 13.5% of total in FY25. First year crossing 1 million annual motorcycle sales (1,002,893 units; 10% from exports). Export momentum strong but FY25 AR does not cite China+1 or supply-chain diversification as a driver — growth attributed to brand premiumization and new international market entries. VECV (Volvo Eicher CV JV) also exports.

inr_exposure.evidence: Royal Enfield export revenue 13.5% of FY25 total (₹2,538 Cr of ₹18,800 Cr consolidated). Export volumes grew ~30% YoY; export share of total units reached 10% in FY25. Markets include Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, and Southeast Asia. FY25 revenue ₹18,800 Cr (+14.1% YoY); EBITDA ₹4,712 Cr; PAT ₹4,734 Cr (+18.3% YoY).

china_plus_one.evidence: Lupin is primarily a formulations company (India 34%, US 38% of revenue). Global API business is only ~5% of revenue. FY25 communications focus on US generics pipeline, domestic brand-building (+13.8% India formulations YoY), and specialty launches — no explicit China+1 attribution found. API sales ₹1,177 Cr (+3.1% YoY). Exports total 66% of consolidated revenue ₹22,192 Cr.

inr_exposure.evidence: US formulation sales USD 925M in FY25 (~38% of ₹22,192 Cr consolidated revenue). India formulation sales ₹7,577 Cr (34%). EMEA 11%, Growth Markets (LatAm/Asia-Pacific) 9%, Other Developed Markets 3%, Global API 5%. Total consolidated revenue ₹22,192 Cr (+12.9% YoY). US revenue primarily USD-denominated.

china_plus_one.evidence: Divi's Laboratories exports 88% of revenue to global pharma companies, primarily Europe (~51%) and US (~12%). Custom synthesis (CRAMS) segment grows through long-term contracts with innovators diversifying API/intermediate sourcing from China to India. FY25 revenue ₹10,560 Cr, PAT ₹2,568 Cr. While 'China+1' is not explicitly named in the AR, strategic positioning as a large-scale API/CRAMS manufacturer clearly serves global pharmaceutical supply chain diversification. Export geographic breakdown from Q1 FY26 data used as FY25 proxy (Europe 58% of exports, US 14% of exports, RoW 28%).

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports 88% of revenue; Europe ~51% of total (EUR-denominated), US ~12% of total (USD-denominated), RoW ~25%. FY25 revenue ₹10,560 Cr. USD-denominated revenue reported at ~12% (US share of exports). European revenue is primarily EUR-denominated and is the largest export destination.

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India serves as a manufacturing hub for ABB Group globally, with intercompany exports (~15% of revenue estimated). Government Make-in-India policy and rising infrastructure capex benefit ABB India's order book. CY2024 revenue ₹12,188 Cr (record, +17% YoY), orders ₹13,079 Cr (record, +21.9% CAGR over 4 years). AR cites data centers, renewable energy, railways, and power distribution as key demand drivers. No explicit 'China+1' framing, but ABB Group's global manufacturing footprint diversification positions India as an alternative production hub.

govt_capex.evidence: ABB India serves government capex-intensive segments: railways (traction systems, signalling), power distribution (transformers, switchgear), renewables (solar inverters, wind systems), metro rail, and water treatment. Government infrastructure capex is a primary demand driver. CY2024 orders ₹13,079 Cr; order backlog ₹9,380 Cr as of Dec-24. Exact government capex revenue % not separately disclosed in available CY2024 AR summary.

inr_exposure.evidence: ABB India exports ~15% of revenue as intercompany supplies to ABB Group globally (estimated — exact % not disclosed in available CY2024 data). Calendar-year reporting company. CY2024 revenue ₹12,188 Cr. EPS ₹88.46 in CY2024 (+50% YoY).

china_plus_one.evidence: Sun Pharma is a global specialty pharma company with 69% of revenue from international markets. US formulation sales USD 1,921M (+3.6% YoY); Global Specialty USD 1,216M (+17.1% YoY); Emerging Markets USD 1,114M (+7% YoY). India's positioning as pharma alternative to China broadly benefits Sun Pharma, but corporate strategy focuses on specialty/branded formulations in regulated markets — not an explicit China+1 API diversification play. Adjusted net profit ₹11,984 Cr (+19% YoY).

inr_exposure.evidence: US formulation sales USD 1,921M in FY25 (~31% of total consolidated revenue). India formulations ~31% (₹4,213 Cr in Q4 FY25 annualised). EMEA ~9%, Emerging Markets (Asia/LatAm/RoW) ~17%, other ~12%. International sales ~69% of total consolidated revenue. Global Specialty portfolio (Ilumya, Cequa, Winlevi) growing rapidly.

rural.evidence: DMart operates 424 stores (as of Jun-25) across 17.6 mn sq. ft. in 10 states, predominantly in urban and semi-urban Tier 1 and Tier 2 city locations. Cluster-based expansion strategy focuses on high-density urban catchments. FY25 revenue ₹57,790 Cr (+16.7% YoY), net profit ₹2,927 Cr (+8.6%), EBITDA margin 7.9%. Not a rural-oriented retailer; rural exposure not material.

inr_exposure.evidence: 100% domestic Indian retail chain. All revenue INR-denominated. No USD or foreign currency exposure. FY25 revenue ₹57,790 Cr.

china_plus_one.evidence: KSB India exports ~17% of total order intake, positioning India as a global manufacturing hub for KSB Group. FY25 total sales revenue ₹2,696 Cr (+6.42% YoY), net profit ₹264.5 Cr (+9.8% YoY), 220% dividend. No explicit China+1 narrative. Domestic growth driven by solar, building services, energy, and water segments. Export business is intercompany supply to KSB Group parent (Germany).

govt_capex.evidence: KSB serves government-funded water supply, irrigation, and solar pump projects. FY25 orders received from Maharashtra State Electricity, MPUVNL (Madhya Pradesh), DGVCL (Gujarat), Department of Horticulture Rajasthan for solar pumps. Water and wastewater sector supported by government Jal Jeevan Mission and AMRUT are key demand drivers. Exact government capex % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~17% of order intake as global manufacturing hub for KSB Group (Germany). FY25 total revenue ₹2,696 Cr. Regional breakdown of exports not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin Point exports ~97% of revenue, primarily to Latin America (76%) and Africa (6%), with regulated US markets accounting for ~18%. Positioned as reliable low-cost Indian pharma exporter for underserved emerging markets. No explicit China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative — growth driven by market penetration in LatAm, Africa, and regulated market expansion (US ANDA filings). FY25 revenue ~₹1,917 Cr (estimated from FY26 ₹2,303 Cr; FY26 PAT ₹650 Cr, +20.1% YoY).

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports 97% of revenue. Latin America 76% of total revenue (mix of USD and local currencies — many LatAm countries peg to or trade in USD). US regulated market ~17% of total (USD-denominated). Africa 6% (mix). Domestic India ~3%. USD revenue % represents primarily US market + USD-denominated LatAm contracts.

china_plus_one.evidence: Navin Fluorine management explicitly states in investor communications that global pharma and agrochem companies seek India as alternative fluorochemical supply base to China, with customers willing to pay a premium for India-sourced products. Company targets 70-80% domestic production to ensure no China dependency for US-bound products. Chemours (US) collaboration announced 2025 for new liquid cooling products. Specialty Chemicals segment grew 21.4% YoY in Q4 FY25; CRAMS grew 15.8% YoY to ₹88 Cr in Q4 FY25. Revenue ₹2,393 Cr FY25 (grew to ₹3,379 Cr FY26, +41%). China+1 tailwind explicitly cited in management communications as a structural order growth driver.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports 77% of revenue (Q4 FY25: exports 77%, domestic 23%). FY25 revenue ₹2,393 Cr; segments: Specialty Chemicals ~40%, CRAMS ~25%, Refrigerants/Inorganic Fluorides ~35%. Export customers are primarily US and European pharma/agrochem companies (USD/EUR denominated). Regional sub-breakdown not disclosed in available data.

china_plus_one.evidence: Gabriel India is primarily an automotive OEM supplier for the domestic Indian market (shock absorbers, suspension systems). Export sales small (~5-7%) but growing rapidly (H1 FY26: exports +59.5% YoY, from a small base). No China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative in available FY25 data. FY25 revenue ₹4,063 Cr. Primary OEM customers: Hero MotoCorp, TVS, Bajaj Auto, Maruti Suzuki, commercial vehicle OEMs.

crude_exposure.evidence: Gabriel manufactures suspension systems using steel tubes, hydraulic oil, and rubber seals — all with some crude/petrochemical linkage. Rubber (seals, bushings) and hydraulic oil are crude-derivative inputs. Exact crude-linked raw material % not disclosed in available FY25 data.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~5-7% of revenue (growing: H1 FY26 up 59.5% YoY from small base). FY25 total revenue ₹4,063 Cr. Aftermarket business also growing (+8.5%). Two-wheeler OEM is largest segment; also serves commercial vehicles and railways.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABSLAMC is an AMC; revenues are fee-based on AUM. Interest rate changes affect fund flows between equity and debt categories, thus affecting AUM and fee income. Falling rates typically boost debt fund AUM and equity market performance; rising rates may redirect retail savings to fixed deposits. Company has minimal own debt. FY25 revenue ₹1,845 Cr, PAT ₹975 Cr. Average AUM ₹4.25 lakh Cr (overall including alternates ₹4.61 lakh Cr, +15% YoY). Investor folios 1.07 Cr (Sep-25). 91% dividend payout.

inr_exposure.evidence: 100% domestic Asset Management Company. All revenue INR-denominated mutual fund management fees. No USD or foreign currency exposure. FY25 revenue ₹1,845 Cr.

china_plus_one.evidence: Kirloskar Brothers International B.V. (Netherlands subsidiary) contributed 33.97% of FY25 consolidated revenue, growing 21.3% YoY. International business is an organic global operation (operations in Netherlands, South Africa, Germany, and other markets) — not a China+1 supply-chain diversification play. FY25 consolidated revenue ₹4,538 Cr; standalone ₹2,828 Cr. Recommended final dividend ₹7/share (350%).

govt_capex.evidence: Kirloskar Brothers is the world's largest pump manufacturer by installed capacity. Core businesses: water supply and sewage treatment (government-funded), power plant cooling (utilities), irrigation systems, and hydro turbines. Government infrastructure projects (both domestic and international public sector) are the dominant revenue driver. Consolidated revenue ₹4,538 Cr FY25. Exact govt capex % not separately disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International B.V. revenue constitutes 33.97% of FY25 consolidated revenue (~₹1,543 Cr estimated). Operations in Netherlands, South Africa, Germany, and other global markets. Consolidated revenue ₹4,538 Cr; standalone ₹2,828 Cr. International revenues in EUR, ZAR, and USD.

rate_sensitive.evidence: IHCL has expanded aggressively (630 hotels, 255 in pipeline globally). Hotel companies typically carry significant debt for property acquisition and renovation; floating rate borrowings affect interest costs. Floating rate liability % not separately disclosed in available FY25 data. FY25 consolidated revenue ₹8,565 Cr (+12% YoY), EBITDA ₹3,000 Cr (35% margin), PAT ₹1,413 Cr standalone (+29% YoY).

inr_exposure.evidence: IHCL consolidated revenue ₹8,565 Cr vs standalone ₹5,145 Cr (India entity only) in FY25. International subsidiaries (Taj Boston, Taj St. James Court London, Taj Palm Dubai, Campton Place San Francisco, etc.) account for estimated ~40% of consolidated revenue (derived from standalone vs consolidated gap, which includes both domestic hotel SPVs and international operations). Portfolio spans 14 countries across 4 continents.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bosch India exports ~30% of revenue as intercompany supplies to Bosch Group globally (estimated; exact % not separately disclosed). India is positioned as a global manufacturing hub for multiple Bosch product lines (fuel injection systems, automotive electronics, power tools). FY25 revenue ₹18,000 Cr (+8.1% YoY), PAT ₹2,000 Cr (11.1% margin). Powertrain Solutions division export sales grew YoY. Bosch targets up to 8% annual growth through 2030 with India as a key production base. No explicit China+1 framing but consistent with global manufacturing diversification into India.

inr_exposure.evidence: Bosch India exports ~30% of revenue as intercompany supplies to Bosch Group globally (estimated). FY25 revenue ₹18,000 Cr (+8.1% YoY). Domestic Mobility sector sales +6.2%; Powertrain Solutions +5.8% (including export growth); Mobility Aftermarket +8.4%; Beyond Mobility +4.4%. Bosch India follows April-March fiscal year. Export revenue primarily EUR-denominated (Bosch HQ Germany).

FSN E-Commerce (Nykaa) is a 100% domestic Indian beauty and fashion e-commerce platform. GMV ₹11,775 Cr in FY25 (+30% YoY). 42mn+ cumulative customers; 237 beauty retail stores (50 added in FY25); largest beauty retail network in India. Beauty 75.5% of GMV, Fashion 24.4%. All revenue INR-denominated.
